The *Rajjumālāvimānavatthu* (Vv 50) is a text of the *Vimānavatthu* collection. The narrative relates the account of a female deity (*deva*) who recounts having been on the verge of suicide before the compassionate Buddha came to her assistance. Six modern translations across six languages are registered for this text.

 It shares substantial verse material with its commentary, the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* (44 matches, including §8.1–31.6) [DharmaNexus]. Substantial formulaic reuse is also found in other *Vimānavatthu* discourses, notably *Vihāravimānavatthu* (Vv 44, §0.1–7.4), *Pāricchattakavimānavatthu* (Vv 38, §2.1–7.4), and *Dāsivimānavatthu* (Vv 18, §24.1–30.6), as well as the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* and the *Abhijjamānapetavatthu* (Pv 26, §28.2–30.6) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language matches, DharmaNexus automatically aligns the text with Tibetan works, displaying the strongest match with the *Ārya-saddharmānusmṛtyupasthāna* (D0287-2) [DharmaNexus].
